Chair of the UNSC Taliban Sanctions Committee and Vice-Chair of FATF
x: Pakistan was chosen to chair the UNSC Taliban Sanctions Committee and to serve as Vice-Chair of the Counter-Terrorism Committee. FATF and UNOCT are organisations with which the CTC works, but Pakistan's stated roles were not chairmanships of those organisations.

s: At the Doha emergency summit in September 2025, which country pushed for a NATO-style “Arab-Islamic task force” after the strike on Hamas leaders in Doha?
x: Pakistan pushed the proposal for a NATO-style Arab-Islamic task force. Turkey’s President attended the summit, but Turkey preferred economic sanctions rather than military action.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about developments concerning Pakistan and India in 2025?
o: India's Operation Sindoor followed the Pahalgam attack of 22 April 2025
Pakistan announced ₹14 crore compensation to families of terrorists
The IMF gave Pakistan a $1 billion loan under a $7 billion facility
Pakistan was added to the FATF grey list in October 2022
x: Pakistan was removed from, not added to, the FATF grey list in October 2022.

s: Pakistan, described at the Doha emergency summit as the only nuclear-armed Muslim nation, holds about how many warheads?
x: Pakistan was described as the only nuclear-armed Muslim nation, with about 170 warheads.

s: At the Doha emergency summit of September 2025, Turkey preferred which response to Israel's strike?
x: Turkey preferred economic sanctions; Pakistan pushed the NATO-style 'Arab-Islamic task force'.

s: Which of the following is NOT a formal partner of the UN Counter-Terrorism Committee?
x: The CTC works with UNOCT, FATF and UN sanctions committees; the IMF is not a formal CTC partner.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Doha emergency summit of September 2025:
1. It was held after Israel's strike on Hamas leaders in Doha.
2. Over 40 Arab and Islamic nations took part.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: 40+ Arab and Islamic nations met in Doha after Israel's strike on Hamas leaders there.

s: When was Pakistan removed from the FATF grey list?
x: Pakistan left the FATF grey list in October 2022.

s: Which office handles delisting requests under the UNSC 1267 sanctions regime?
x: The 1267 regime has an Ombudsperson for delisting; the committee of all 15 UNSC members decides by consensus.

s: Which office handles delisting requests under the UN Security Council 1267 sanctions regime?
o: UN High Commissioner for Human Rights
x: The 1267 regime (Al-Qaida, Taliban, ISIL) has an Ombudsperson for delisting.

s: Which country was admitted as an 'SCO Partner' at the SCO Summit 2025, taking the total to 10 members and 17 partners?
x: Laos was admitted as a partner after observer and dialogue partner categories were merged into 'SCO Partner'.

s: Which attack in Jammu and Kashmir did the SCO Summit 2025 Tianjin Declaration condemn?
x: The declaration condemned the 22 April Pahalgam attack, along with the Jaffer Express and Khuzdar attacks in Pakistan.

s: What position on Iran was recorded in the Tianjin Declaration of the SCO Summit 2025?
o: It endorsed the US–Israel strikes and rejected UNSC Resolution 2231
It condemned the US–Israel strikes on Iran’s nuclear facilities and reaffirmed UNSC Resolution 2231
It condemned the Pahalgam attack and reaffirmed the Bandung principles
It supported the Belt and Road Initiative and rejected UNSC Resolution 2231
x: The declaration condemned the US–Israel strikes on Iran’s nuclear facilities in June 2025 and reaffirmed United Nations Security Council Resolution 2231. The other options reverse or replace these positions with unrelated issues.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's position at the SCO Summit 2025 (Tianjin Declaration)?
o: India endorsed the Belt and Road Initiative
India did not endorse CPEC through PoK
Modi described the Ukraine issue as 'it is humanity's call'
India refused to endorse the Belt and Road Initiative
x: India refused to endorse the BRI, including CPEC through PoK.

s: For which time did China host the SCO summit at Tianjin (25th SCO Summit)?
x: China hosted the SCO summit for the 5th time at Tianjin in 2025.

s: What was the theme of the 25th SCO Summit at Tianjin?
o: Upholding the Shanghai Spirit: SCO on the Move
25 Years of the SCO: Together for Sustainable Peace
x: The Tianjin summit theme was 'Upholding the Shanghai Spirit: SCO on the Move'.

s: Which initiative did Xi Jinping propose at the 2025 SCO Summit?
x: Xi proposed the Global Governance Initiative (GGI) and an SCO Development Bank at Tianjin.

s: Where is the SCO's counter-terrorism body RATS located?
x: RATS is located in Tashkent; India and Pakistan became full SCO members in 2017.

s: Which two categories were merged into a single 'SCO Partner' status at the 25th SCO Summit at Tianjin (2025)?
x: The Tianjin summit merged the observer and dialogue partner categories into a single 'SCO Partner' status.

s: For which time did China host the SCO summit at Tianjin in 2025?
x: The 25th SCO Summit at Tianjin (2025) was the fifth time China hosted the SCO summit.

s: Which outcome was associated with the Modi–Xi meeting on the sidelines of the SCO Summit 2025 in Tianjin?
o: Suspension of direct flights and rejection of Panchsheel principles
Admission of Laos as a full SCO member and creation of the SCO Development Bank
Revival of Panchsheel principles and resumption of direct India–China flights after about five years
Signing of the Panchsheel Agreement and establishment of RATS
x: The meeting was associated with the revival of Panchsheel principles and the resumption of direct flights between India and China after about five years. The other options either reverse the outcomes or combine them with unrelated SCO developments.

s: In which year were the Panchsheel principles signed on 29 April?
x: Panchsheel was signed on 29 April 1954, not 1955; India reopened tourist visas for Chinese nationals in July 2025.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: RATS, the SCO's counter-terrorism body, is in Tashkent, so that pair is correct. Panchsheel was signed in 1954, the Bandung Conference was in 1955 and the UNGA resolution on peaceful coexistence was adopted in 1957.

s: In which year did the UN General Assembly adopt a Panchsheel-based resolution?
x: The UNGA adopted a Panchsheel-based resolution in 1957; the 1961 Belgrade NAM Conference treated Panchsheel as NAM's core.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India–China air connectivity?
o: Direct flights were suspended from January 2020.
Fewer than 20 weekly flights operated before 2020.
The suspension was linked to COVID-19 and later Galwan tensions.
Direct flights resumed after about five years following the Modi–Xi meeting at Tianjin.
x: Over 80 weekly flights operated between India and China before 2020.

s: At which conference were the Panchsheel principles included in the Ten Principles?
x: The Bandung Conference of 1955 (29 Afro-Asian countries) included Panchsheel in its Ten Principles.

s: In the preamble of which agreement were the Panchsheel principles signed on 29 April 1954?
o: Agreement on Trade and Intercourse between the Tibet Region of China and India
x: Panchsheel was set out in the preamble of the 1954 Agreement on Trade and Intercourse between the Tibet Region of China and India.

s: Which countries sponsored the 1957 UN General Assembly resolution on peaceful coexistence based on Panchsheel?
x: The 1957 UNGA resolution on peaceful coexistence was moved by India, Yugoslavia and Sweden and was adopted.

s: To which year does the ASEAN-India Trade in Goods Agreement (AITIGA) date?
x: AITIGA for goods dates to 2010; its services component dates to 2015.

s: Who is José Ramos-Horta?
x: Ramos-Horta is the President of Timor-Leste, ASEAN's 11th member, not ASEAN's Secretary-General.

s: Which two ASEAN members expressed reservations about Timor-Leste's membership?
x: Singapore and Myanmar expressed reservations about Timor-Leste's membership.

s:
Arrange the following milestones in Timor-Leste’s path towards ASEAN membership in chronological order:
1. Timor-Leste applied for ASEAN membership.
2. Timor-Leste achieved independence.
3. Timor-Leste received “in-principle” admission.
4. Timor-Leste signed the ASEAN Treaty of Amity and Cooperation.
x: The correct sequence is independence in 2002, signing the ASEAN Treaty of Amity and Cooperation in 2007, applying for membership in 2011, and receiving “in-principle” admission in 2022. The other sequences disturb this timeline.

s: Which country hosted the 47th ASEAN Summit at which the Prime Minister of India delivered a virtual address?
x: The 47th ASEAN Summit was held in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, and the Prime Minister addressed it virtually. Jakarta is the headquarters of ASEAN, while Indonesia, Singapore and Timor-Leste are associated with ASEAN but were not the venue identified for this summit.

s: In which year did Indonesia invade Timor-Leste?
x: Indonesia invaded Timor-Leste in 1975; the New York Agreements followed in 1999.

s: In which area has 2026 been declared the Year of ASEAN-India cooperation?
x: 2026 is the Year of ASEAN–India Maritime Cooperation; the ASEAN Community Vision 2045 is linked with Viksit Bharat 2047.

s: Which of the following India–ASEAN milestone–year pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: The summit-level partnership began in 2002, not 2012; the strategic partnership dates to 2012.

s: As part of which ASEAN Summit was the 22nd ASEAN-India Summit held virtually?
x: The 22nd ASEAN–India Summit was part of the 47th ASEAN Summit at Kuala Lumpur.

s: How many members does the East Asia Summit now have?
x: The EAS has 19 members: 11 ASEAN members and 8 partners.

s: Which declaration did the 20th East Asia Summit at Kuala Lumpur in 2025 adopt?
x: The 20th EAS adopted the Kuala Lumpur Declaration on peace and stability in the Indo-Pacific.

s: Admission criteria for new ASEAN members are laid down in which Article of the ASEAN Charter?
x: Admission criteria are in Article 6 of the ASEAN Charter; Timor-Leste became the 11th member.

s:
Consider the following statements about ASEAN:
1. It was founded on 8 August 1967.
2. Its headquarters is in Jakarta.
3. Its 60th anniversary falls in 2027.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: All three are correct: ASEAN was founded on 8 August 1967, is headquartered in Jakarta and turns 60 in 2027.

s: What was the theme of the 47th ASEAN Summit held at Kuala Lumpur in October 2025?
x: Malaysia chaired the 47th ASEAN Summit at Kuala Lumpur with the theme 'Inclusivity and Sustainability'.

s: Which of the following was NOT a founder member of ASEAN in 1967?
x: ASEAN's founders were Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore and Thailand; Brunei joined later.

s: In which year and city was the East Asia Summit founded?
x: The East Asia Summit was founded in 2005 at Kuala Lumpur; its chair rotates annually among ASEAN members.

s: In which year did Timor-Leste become independent?
x: Timor-Leste became independent in 2002, after the New York Agreements of 1999; it became ASEAN's 11th member in 2025.

s: When was the ASEAN Community Vision 2045 adopted?
x: ASEAN Community Vision 2045 was adopted in May 2025 and is linked with India's Viksit Bharat 2047.

s: In which year was the 80th session of the UN General Assembly held?
x: The UN was founded in 1945 and its 80th General Assembly session was in 2025.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Beijing+30 High-Level Meeting at the UN?
o: It marked the 35th anniversary of the Fourth World Conference on Women
The Beijing Declaration and Platform for Action dates to 1995
It was held in New York
It called for universal ratification of CEDAW
x: Beijing+30 marked the 30th anniversary, not the 35th, of the Fourth World Conference on Women.

s: Universal ratification of which convention did the Beijing+30 High-Level Meeting on women's rights call for?
o: the Convention on the Rights of the Child
x: The Beijing+30 meeting called for universal ratification of CEDAW.

s: What did the 78th World Health Assembly adopt in May 2025?
x: The 78th WHA adopted the world's first WHO Pandemic Agreement by consensus on 20 May 2025.

s: Where was the Third UN Ocean Conference (UNOC3) held in June 2025?
x: UNOC3 was held at Nice, France, co-hosted by France and Costa Rica.

s: With which document did the Third UN Ocean Conference close?
x: UNOC3 adopted the Nice Ocean Action Plan in support of SDG 14.

s: Where was COP30 of the UNFCCC held in November 2025?
x: COP30 was held at Belém, Brazil, and closed with the 'Global Mutirão' decision.

s: What finance path for developing countries was agreed at COP30?
x: COP30 set a path of USD 1.3 trillion a year by 2035 and called for tripling adaptation finance.

s:
Consider the following statements about COP30 at Belém:
1. It closed with the 'Global Mutirão' decision.
2. Its final text included a fossil-fuel transition roadmap.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: COP30 closed with the Global Mutirão decision, but the final text had no fossil-fuel transition roadmap.

s: Which two countries co-hosted the Third UN Ocean Conference at Nice in June 2025?
x: UNOC3 (Nice, 9-13 June 2025) was co-hosted by France and Costa Rica and ended with the Nice Ocean Action Plan.

s: By what name is the final decision of COP30 at Belém known?
x: COP30 at Belém, Brazil (November 2025) closed with the 'Global Mutirão' decision.

s: Which Sustainable Development Goal does the Nice Ocean Action Plan of the Third UN Ocean Conference support?
x: The Nice Ocean Action Plan (UNOC3, June 2025) supports SDG 14, Life below Water.

s: At which COP did India announce its 'Panchamrit' climate pledges?
x: India's Panchamrit climate commitments were announced at COP26, Glasgow (2021).

s: In which year were the Beijing Declaration and Platform for Action adopted?
x: They were adopted at the Fourth World Conference on Women in 1995; Beijing+30 marked the 30th anniversary in 2025.

s: Which UN agency organises the AI for Good Global Summit, held in Geneva on 8-11 July 2025?
x: The AI for Good Global Summit is organised by the ITU and held in Geneva.

s: Which corridor is presented as India's alternative to China's Belt and Road Initiative?
x: The India–Middle East–Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC) is presented as India's alternative to BRI.

s: What action did the US take on products refined from Russian oil, including those re-exported by India?
x: The US imposed tariffs on products refined from Russian oil, including those re-exported by India.

s: From what did the term 'G-2' for the US-China relationship first originate?
x: The term first came from Obama–Hu Jintao in 2009; Trump did not coin it at Busan.

s: From which date did Trump announce a 100% tariff on all Chinese goods?
x: The 100% tariff was announced from 1 November 2025, after China's 9 October export controls.

s: Regarding the Trump–Xi Busan summit and US tariffs, which pair is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Truce on tariffs and rare-earth export curbs – One year
US tariffs on Chinese imports – Cut to 47%
x: India faced 50% tariffs (25% retaliatory plus 25% Russia-oil levy); 47% is the cut rate on Chinese imports.

s: How was India characterised in the debate over US tariffs on products refined from Russian oil?
o: A force for equilibrium between the West and the Global South
A leader of an anti-Western bloc
A member of the Western alliance
A neutral bystander in global trade
x: India was viewed as a force for equilibrium between the West and the Global South.

s: On the sidelines of which forum did the Trump-Xi meeting at Busan on 30 October 2025 take place?
x: Trump and Xi met in Busan, South Korea, on the sidelines of APEC.

s: To what level were US tariffs on Chinese imports cut after the Busan summit?
x: US tariffs on China were cut to 47%; India and Brazil face the highest US tariffs at 50%.

s: Under which President of China did Wen Jiabao serve as Premier from 2003 to 2013?
x: Wen Jiabao was China's Premier from 2003 to 2013 under President Hu Jintao.

s: Which Mauritius Prime Minister attended the Ganga Aarti and visited Kashi Vishwanath Dham during the Varanasi engagement?
x: Prime Minister Navinchandra Ramgoolam attended the Ganga Aarti and visited Kashi Vishwanath Dham.

s: In which year did Modi and Albanese launch the India-Australia Renewable Energy Partnership?
x: The partnership was launched in 2024, not 2023; Chris Bowen visited New Delhi in October 2025.

s: What was the revised target deadline for PM-KUSUM mentioned in September 2025?
x: The PM-KUSUM target was revised to March 2026 and may be extended. The other options change the deadline or the possibility of extension.

s: By how much below 2005 levels is Australia's 2035 emissions-reduction target?
x: Australia's 2035 target is a 62–70% cut below 2005 levels, with net zero by 2050.

s: Through which organisation will India showcase PM-KUSUM and PM Surya Ghar in Africa and island nations?
x: India will showcase PM-KUSUM and PM Surya Ghar through the International Solar Alliance.

s: Which distinctive feature of Kalmykia was highlighted during the exposition of the Sacred Relics of Lord Buddha?
o: It is the only European territory where Hinduism is the main religion
It is the only European territory where Islam is the main religion
It is the only European territory where Buddhism is the main religion
It is the only European territory where Christianity is the main religion
x: Kalmykia is the only European territory where Buddhism is the main religion. The alternatives incorrectly replace Buddhism with Islam, Hinduism or Christianity.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about PM-KUSUM?
o: It includes solarisation of 35 lakh grid-connected pumps
By September 2025, decentralised solar plants had reached about 6%
By September 2025, standalone solar pumps had reached about 25%
x: By September 2025 standalone solar pumps had reached about 70%, not 25% (16–25% is the figure for grid-connected pumps). PM-KUSUM was launched in 2019, covers solarising 35 lakh grid-connected pumps, and decentralised plants reached about 6%.

s: What is India's target for non-fossil installed capacity by 2030?
x: India targets 500 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030 (including 280 GW of solar) and reached 50% non-fossil installed capacity in July 2025.

s: Which institutions organised the exposition of the Sacred Relics of Lord Buddha in Kalmykia?
o: The Ministry of Culture, International Buddhist Confederation, National Museum and IGNCA
The Ministry of Culture, ASEAN, National Museum and the Joint Rivers Commission
The International Buddhist Confederation, UNESCO, IGNCA and the Joint Rivers Commission
The National Museum, Thousand Talents Programme, IGNCA and ASEAN
x: The organisers were the Ministry of Culture, International Buddhist Confederation, National Museum and IGNCA. ASEAN, the Joint Rivers Commission and the Thousand Talents Programme were not identified as organisers of this exposition.

s: The Kalmykia exposition recalled which Buddhist figure who revived Buddhism in Mongolia, Kalmykia, Buryatia and Tuva?
x: The 19th Kushok Bakula Rinpoche revived Buddhism in Mongolia, Kalmykia, Buryatia and Tuva.

s: In which country did India's 2025 special economic package set up the first Jan Aushadhi Kendra outside India?
x: The package for Mauritius, announced at Varanasi on 11 September 2025, includes the first Jan Aushadhi Kendra outside India and a 500-bed hospital.

s: The India–Mauritius engagement in September 2025 was guided by which pair of Indian policy frameworks?
o: Make in India and Digital India
x: The engagement was guided by the Neighbourhood First and SAGAR policies. The other pairs are not the policy frameworks identified for this India–Mauritius engagement.

s: What was signed during the 9th India–South Africa Joint Defence Committee meeting held in Johannesburg in June 2025?
o: An agreement on Defence Policy and Military Cooperation
An agreement on Defence Acquisition, Production and R&D
A new BRICS, IORA, IBSA and NAM grouping
x: India and South Africa signed two agreements on submarine cooperation during the 9th Joint Defence Committee meeting in Johannesburg. Defence Policy and Military Cooperation and Defence Acquisition, Production and R&D were the names of sub-committees, while BRICS, IORA, IBSA and NAM were shared groupings.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the India–South Africa 9th Joint Defence Committee meeting?
o: Defence Policy & Military Cooperation was one of the sub-committees
Defence Acquisition, Production, R&D was one of the sub-committees
The Defence Acquisition, Production, R&D sub-committee was replaced by the Defence Policy & Military Cooperation sub-committee
India and South Africa share membership of BRICS, IORA, IBSA and NAM
x: The two sub-committees were separate; neither replaced the other.

s: When did India reach 50% non-fossil installed capacity, five years ahead of the 2030 goal?
x: India reached 50% non-fossil installed capacity in July 2025, five years early.

s: What is the capital of Kalmykia, where the Sacred Relics of Lord Buddha were exhibited in 2025?
x: The relics were shown at Elista, capital of Kalmykia, the only European territory where Buddhism is the main religion.

s: Of India's 500 GW non-fossil target for 2030, how much is to come from solar?
x: India aims at 500 GW non-fossil capacity by 2030, with 280 GW from solar.

s: How many standalone solar pumps are to be installed under PM-KUSUM (2019)?
x: PM-KUSUM: 100 GW solar on farm land, 14 lakh standalone pumps and solarising 35 lakh grid-connected pumps.

s: What kind of European-led force did Europe plan at the August 2025 summit on Ukraine?
x: Europe planned a European-led 'reassurance force' and sought US security guarantees; NATO membership was ruled out.

s: The Russia–Ukraine war discussed at the August 2025 summit began in which month and year?
x: The war began in February 2022. August 2025 was the month of the summit, not the beginning of the war.

s: Which historian used the term 'Axis of Upheaval' in 2009 for unstable states?
x: Niall Ferguson used it in 2009; Kendall-Taylor and Fontaine popularised it in Foreign Affairs in April 2024.

s: Which elite military unit seized power in Madagascar after the National Assembly impeached President Andry Rajoelina?
x: CAPSAT seized power after the National Assembly impeached President Andry Rajoelina. TTP and PTM are organisations associated with Pakistan, while SADC is a regional bloc.

s: What were the main triggers behind the youth-led protests that preceded the Madagascar political crisis?
o: A military pay dispute and a drought emergency
A disputed maritime boundary and a currency collapse
Food exports and a parliamentary boycott
x: Power and water shortages triggered the youth-led protests. The other alternatives introduce causes not identified in the crisis facts.

s: Madagascar, whose capital is Antananarivo, belongs to which regional bloc?
x: Madagascar's regional bloc is SADC; the African Union was likely to suspend it.

s: The Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD), Africa's largest hydroelectric project, is on which river?
x: GERD lies on the Blue Nile near the Sudan border, with a storage capacity of 74 billion cubic metres.

s: What is the installed capacity of the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD)?
x: GERD has an installed capacity of 5,150 MW, with storage of 74 billion cubic metres.

s: Which countries does CRINK, the 'Axis of Upheaval' discussed around the SCO Summit 2025, refer to?
o: China, Russia, India and North Korea
Cuba, Russia, Iran and North Korea
China, Russia, Iran and North Korea
China, Russia, Iraq and North Korea
x: CRINK denotes China, Russia, Iran and North Korea, an informal alignment rather than a formal alliance like NATO.

s: The August 2025 White House summit on the Ukraine peace process was preceded by which meeting?
x: The White House summit was preceded by a meeting between Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin in Alaska. The Brussels meeting was not identified as the preceding event.

s: Which position did Russia reportedly take in discussions on ending the Ukraine war in August 2025?
o: Control over Donbas while freezing the southern frontline
Withdrawal from Donbas while reopening the southern frontline
European control over Donbas while freezing the northern frontline
Ukraine’s NATO membership while retaining the southern frontline
x: Russia demanded control over Donbas and was willing to freeze the southern frontline. The alternatives alter either the territory, the frontline, or the NATO position.

s: Which two analysts popularised the term CRINK in Foreign Affairs in April 2024?
x: Kendall-Taylor and Fontaine (CNAS) popularised CRINK in 2024; Niall Ferguson used 'Axis of Upheaval' in 2009.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD)?
o: It is on the Blue Nile
It lies near the Kenya border
x: GERD is on the Blue Nile near the Sudan border, not Kenya.

s: Who inaugurated the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam, Africa's largest hydroelectric project?
x: Ethiopian PM Abiy Ahmed inaugurated GERD on the Blue Nile (5,150 MW).

s: Which countries co-hosted the 3rd UN Ocean Conference held at Nice in June 2025?
x: The 3rd UN Ocean Conference was held at Nice, France, in June 2025 and was co-hosted by France and Costa Rica.

s: Which of the following event – venue pairs is correctly matched?
o: Summit for a New Global Financing Pact – Goa
Summit for a New Global Financing Pact – Paris
x: The Summit for a New Global Financing Pact was in Paris; the MI-8 Ministerial was in Goa and the Global Pulse Confederation conclave in India.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: The One Health Summit 2026 was held in Lyon, France, under the G7 Presidency; it was not held in Geneva. The other pairs are correctly matched.

s: Where was the Summit for a New Global Financing Pact (22–23 June 2023) held?
x: The Summit for a New Global Financing Pact was held at Paris in June 2023.

s: Where was the One Health Summit 2026, under France's G7 Presidency, held?
x: The One Health Summit 2026 was at Lyon, not Geneva; Nice hosted the UN Ocean Conference.

s: Where was the IPCC meeting of May 2007 on climate change mitigation, held in the lead-up to the Fourth Assessment Report, held?
x: The IPCC working group on mitigation met at Bangkok in May 2007, ahead of the Fourth Assessment Report.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Ocean Conference:
1. Its 9th edition was held in Mauritius in April 2026.
2. It was started in 2016 by the India Foundation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: the 9th Indian Ocean Conference was in Mauritius (April 2026), and the series was started in 2016 by the India Foundation.

s: Where was the 5th India-Arab Partnership Conference, organised with FICCI and the League of Arab States, held?
x: The 5th India-Arab Partnership Conference was held in Dubai, organised with FICCI and the League of Arab States.

s: Where was the Mission Innovation (MI-8) clean energy ministerial of July 2023 held?
x: The MI-8 ministerial on clean energy was held at Goa in July 2023.

s: Where did the World Council of Religious Leaders meet in June 2002, after the UN Millennium World Peace Summit?
x: The World Council of Religious Leaders met in Bangkok in June 2002, following the Millennium World Peace Summit of 2000.

s: Who organised the New Delhi World Book Fair 2017, whose theme was 'Manushi'?
x: The New Delhi World Book Fair 2017 was organised by the National Book Trust; its theme Manushi covered writings on and by women.

s: Where was the 77th session of the Indian History Congress (2016) held?
x: The 77th Indian History Congress (2016) was held at Thiruvananthapuram, hosted by the University of Kerala.

s: Where was the International Ayurveda Congress 2017 held?
x: The International Ayurveda Congress 2017 was held in London.

s: What was the theme of India Mobile Congress 2025, held at Yashobhoomi, New Delhi?
x: India Mobile Congress 2025 (8-11 Oct 2025, Yashobhoomi, New Delhi) had the theme 'Innovate to Transform'.

s: The WEF Annual Meeting 2025, held at Davos, focused primarily on which of the following?
o: Global digital taxation and cryptocurrency regulation
x: The WEF Annual Meeting 2025 at Davos focused on AI governance and climate change.

s: How many members does the Board of Peace, launched at the WEF Davos meeting in January 2026, have?
x: The Board of Peace has 27 members; it was launched by the US President for Gaza reconstruction, with India only an observer.

s: The Davos Compact on Antimicrobial Resistance was launched at which event?
x: The Davos Compact on Antimicrobial Resistance was launched at the WEF Annual Meeting 2026 in Davos.

s: Where was the WEF 'Summer Davos' (Annual Meeting of the New Champions) of June 2026 held?
x: Summer Davos was held at Dalian, China; Davos hosts the WEF Annual Meeting.

s: What was the theme of the World Economic Forum Annual Meeting at Davos in 2017, attended by Xi Jinping?
o: Creating a Shared Future in a Fractured World
x: WEF Davos 2017 had the theme 'Responsive and Responsible Leadership' and was attended by Chinese President Xi Jinping.

s: The theme of the 20th G20 Summit hosted by South Africa in 2025 was associated with which of the following?
o: Working Together to Address Major International Challenges
Solidarity, Equality, and Sustainability; the spirit of Ubuntu
Inclusivity and Sustainability; ASEAN rotational chairmanship
x: The 20th G20 Summit adopted the theme “Solidarity, Equality, and Sustainability”, reflecting the philosophy of Ubuntu, or “I am because we are.”

s: Where was the 20th G20 Summit (November 2025), the first held on African soil, held?
x: The 20th G20 Summit was held in Johannesburg, South Africa, in November 2025.

s: What does the Africa Skills Multiplier proposed by India envisage?
o: One million solar panels in five years
One million digital health workers in one year
One million trainers in a decade
One million hectares of forest by 2030
x: The Africa Skills Multiplier proposal envisages one million trainers over a decade.

s: What does the G20 Troika comprise?
o: Present presidency and the next two presidencies
Past two presidencies and the present presidency
Present presidency, the IMF and the World Bank
x: The Troika is the past, present and next presidencies; the G20 works through Finance and Sherpa tracks.

s: Which of the following was the headline outcome of the 18th G20 Summit hosted by India?
o: Admission of Timor-Leste as an ASEAN member
Adoption of the Glasgow Climate Pact
Admission of the African Union as a permanent member
